newsitem.title: USA: Hortense watched for Florida landfall - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: Hortense watched for Florida landfall - Smith Barney.

text.p: Hurricane Hortense, moving through the Caribbean near Puerto Rico, could make landfall in south Florida but does not now look likely to head into the Gulf of Mexico, a Smith Barney forecaster said.

"Right now, the probability of Hortense pushing into the Gulf appears to be slim. The probability of it striking south or southwestern Florida is a bit better," said Basilio Lopez, a forecaster for Smith Barney in Chicago.
He said a south Florida landfall would affect citrus, but it does not appear Hortense will affect either offshore Gulf oil rigs or inland cotton fields.

At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the storm was about 135 miles 220 kilometres southeast of Ponce, Puerto Rico as it moved west at six miles per hour (mph)/nine kilometres per hour (kph) while packing sustained winds of 80 mph/130 kph.
Hortense remained a weak Category 1 hurricane, according to National Hurricane Center.
